summary: On a sorted array, two converging pointers answer pair/triple questions in O(N) after the O(N log N) sort — pair-sum, pair-difference, 3-sum, closest pair, container-with-most-water. On a non-negative array, two same-direction pointers form a sliding window for subarray-sum / longest-run problems. The invariant to protect: moving a pointer changes the quantity monotonically.

thoughtProcess.title: Sorted array + 'find a pair/triple' -> opposite-end pointers.
thoughtProcess.body: l=0, r=N-1. If sum too small move l right, too big move r left. Each element visited once -> O(N). Sort first if not sorted.

thoughtProcess.title: Non-negative values + 'subarray sum / longest window' -> same-direction window.
thoughtProcess.body: Expand right to grow the sum, shrink left when it exceeds the target. Only valid when values are non-negative (so growth is monotonic); with negatives use prefix-sum + hashmap.

thoughtProcess.title: 3-sum / 3-pointers = fix one, two-pointer the rest.
thoughtProcess.body: Sort, fix index i, run a two-pointer scan on (i+1 .. N-1). Skip duplicates on i and on the moving pointers to avoid repeat triples.

keyPatterns.name: Opposite-end pointers (sorted)
keyPatterns.when: Pair with target sum/difference, container water, closest pair
keyPatterns.template:
l=0, r=N-1
while l<r: cur=f(A[l],A[r]); update; if cur<target l++ else r--

keyPatterns.name: Fixed-anchor + two pointer
keyPatterns.template: sort; for i: l=i+1,r=N-1; move l/r by comparison; skip dups

keyPatterns.name: Sliding window (non-negative)
keyPatterns.when: Longest run / subarray with sum condition
keyPatterns.template: l=0; for r: add A[r]; while(invalid) remove A[l++]; track best

commonMistakes.title: Two-pointer on an array with negatives
commonMistakes.right: use prefix-sum + hashmap when values can be negative
commonMistakes.why: The window invariant assumes adding grows the sum and removing shrinks it; a negative element breaks monotonicity and skips valid windows.

commonMistakes.title: 3-sum returning duplicate triples
commonMistakes.right: while(l<r && A[l]==A[l-1]) l++; (and same for i, r)
commonMistakes.why: Without skipping equal neighbours you emit the same triple many times.

edgeCases: Empty or single-element array — the l<r loop simply never runs; make sure that returns the right base answer.
All-equal array in 3-sum — duplicate-skipping must still allow the one valid triple.
Pair sum/difference: overflow — A[l]+A[r] with values up to 1e9 needs long.
Difference problems: decide up front whether pairs are ordered and whether a value can pair with itself.
